| | |
|---|---|

## Task
Robot singles badminton on a small court (the BWF court's lengths x 0.4, the net at its BWF height 1.524 m) in real time (slowed down): a Franka Panda arm held to the real Panda's limits, with a racket, on an x-y gantry of ball-screw axes (2 m/s, 15 m/s^2), a point-mass shuttle with the real shuttle's high quadratic drag (terminal speed 6.8 m/s) and no bounce, a racket contact law of gain 4 (shuttles leave the racket at up to about 10 m/s); rally scoring, one game to 11 points; the players' robots serve (the rally winner serves next): the server tosses the shuttle (from rest or rising up to 0.5 m) at a point it chooses and hits it underhand, below 1.15 m, into the diagonal service court; format match-wallclock: you against a scripted computer opponent (levels 1-3, `game spec` match.opponent_level), format duel-wallclock: two players; format `duel-wallclock` (seats A, B),
action level `high`, program play. Generated by `tools/generate.py` from
`sports/badminton/sport.toml`; do not edit by hand.

Deviations from the rulebook:

|---|---|---|

## Difficulty
Set at run time: the seed (`RO_SEED`; it draws the match's random conditions) and the first player (`FIRST_PLAYER`; play both orders).
Official matches use the sport's hidden seed set (seeds per format x level: duel-wallclock: 20, match-wallclock/L1: 20, match-wallclock/L2: 20, match-wallclock/L3: 20; sha256 `648163792ee2bd268c913ee0bddcb8371bfd72d6d71f1347a1ce62fbd850fac6`; `sports/badminton/seed_commitments.json`): the runner gives the sim service one seed of the match's cell and its salt (`RCB_SEED_SALT`), the players never see them, no record shows them (seed -1), and the verifier counts a match as official only when its commitment is in the registered cell (`hidden_seed`, `hidden_seed_index`).
Continuous score `point_share` (larger is better; `<seat>_continuous_score`, and `continuous_score` for a single-side format): your points / all points played in the match (the opponent's or the other player's points included); 0.5 when no point was played; a side that forfeits gets 0.0.

## Reference solution
`solution/solve.sh` runs the sport's reference player (`solution/builtin_players.py`) through the core's client
(`solution/ro_client.py`): camera images and `/spec` only.

## Verification
The `sim` service (the v0.2 core, `environment/sim/core/`) records the match (`episode.jsonl`) and a fresh process
replays it (state hash); the verifier (`tests/grade.py` = `core/grading.py`, no network) writes the common reward
fields (`success`, `valid_trial`, `deterministic`, `<seat>_won`, ...) and the sport's fields (`tests/sport_grade.py`).

## Details
| | |
|---|---|
| Rules | [BWF Laws of Badminton (BWF Statutes, Section 4.1, version 5.0)](https://extranet.bwf.sport/docs/document-system/81/1466/1470/Section%204.1%20-%20Laws%20of%20Badminton%20-%2026%20April%202025%20V5.0%20(2)%20.pdf) version 2025-04-26 |
| id | rule | deviation |
| D1 | 7 | one short game instead of best of three games to 21 (cap 30): first to 11 points (one game of the 5 x 11 scoring BWF has trialled), from 10-10 a two-point lead is needed, at most 15 (14-14: the next point wins); the match also ends after 400 hits (both sides) or 40 points played (lets included): the player ahead wins, at equal points the winner of the last point |
| D2 | 9.1.5-9.1.8 | the robot has no free hand to hold and drop the shuttle: the server tosses it with the command toss {pos: [x, y, z], height: H} (the common racket-sport toss, docs/conventions/racket_serve_zh.md): when the command takes effect the shuttle appears at that point (0.5-1.8 m high, within 1.0 m horizontally of the server's base, on its half) and is released from rest (H = 0) or projected straight up to rise H (at most 0.5 m; the Laws do not forbid a small toss); until then it is held beside the server. The toss has no spin (a point mass has none, Law 9.1.5). Judged: the server's racket must hit it (a miss is a fault, Law 9.1.8), with the shuttle below 1.15 m at the hit (Law 9.1.6, judged at the shuttle's point: it has no size) and leaving the racket upwards (Law 9.1). Not judged: the racket hitting the base of the shuttle first and moving forwards throughout the service (Laws 9.1.5, 9.1.7) |
| D3 | 13.3-13.4 | the shuttle is a point mass: a crossing of the net plane below the net top (between the posts) is a fault of the hitter; touching the net or reaching over it is not judged; a racket meets the shuttle only on its own half and only when it is that player's turn (no double hits) |
| D4 | 9.1.3-9.1.4 | before every serve the referee puts both robots at rest in the ready pose at a fixed spot in their service courts (diagonally opposite: the right courts when the server's score is even, Law 10.1): x = +0.12 (right court) or -0.12 (left court), y = -1.6 in each robot's frame (the legacy spot 0.3 / 4.0 m x 0.4); after the serve there is no automatic return: a base stays where it struck until its player moves it (`move`). Standing still (Law 9.1.4) is judged on the base: a base more than 5 cm from its spot before the serve is delivered (hit, or faulted) is that player's fault; both at once: a let (Law 14.2.2). The base is a real gantry of ball-screw axes (Festo EGC-185-BS-KF-40P, spindle axes EGC-BS-KF technical data: 2.0 m/s, 15 m/s^2, feed force 3000 N, working stroke up to 3000 mm; jerk 25 x the acceleration, estimated; a low-level command is refused beyond its speed and per-axis acceleration) and moves within |x| <= 1.5, -3.53 <= y <= -0.5 |
| D8 | 1.1-1.6, 1.10 | a small court: every line of the BWF court at 0.4 of its length (singles court 2.072 x 5.36 m: side lines at |x| = 1.036, back lines at |y| = 2.68, short service lines 0.792 m from the net, doubles side lines (posts) at |x| = 1.22; the singles back line is also the long service line, as on a singles-only court); the net keeps its BWF height (1.524 m at the centre). Why: with real-robot limits the shuttle leaves the racket at about 10 m/s at most (D9), and the real shuttle's drag (terminal speed 6.8 m/s, kept) carries it about 4-5 m: the 13.40 m court cannot be played (a clear needs 40-50 m/s). The robot is human-sized (its racket meets shuttles 0.4-2.5 m high), so the net is not scaled. No official reduced format is this short (the shortest are the junior mini-badminton courts, about 11.9 m, nets 1.30-1.40 m; wheelchair singles' live depth 4.72 m per side): the scale follows the robot's measured range (docs/benchmarks/badminton-minicourt-20261008.md) |
| D9 | - | the robots: a Franka Panda arm held to the real Panda's joint velocity, acceleration, jerk, torque and torque-rate limits (bodies/franka_panda) on a real gantry (D4); the racket is not simulated as a string bed: a contact law sends the shuttle along the face normal at 4 x the head speed along the normal (a real racket gives about 1.5 x; 4 lets the Panda's best swing, about 4.4 m/s, stand for that of a real fast badminton arm, ANYmal + DynaArm 2025, 10-12 m/s: the real-limits audit's option c) |
| D5 | - | the last resort of the no-draw rule (equal points at the match limit and no point won) is not from the rulebook: the player who received first wins (format match-wallclock: the opponent) |
| D6 | 9.1.1, 16.6-16.7 | undue delay has a fixed limit: the server must toss the shuttle within 3 s after the receiver is ready (1 s after play resumes, Law 9.4), else it is a service fault (the receiver wins the rally: its point and the next serve); every undue delay is such a fault, never a disqualification, instead of the umpire's warning and the referee's discretion (Laws 16.7.1-16.7.2) |
| D7 | 6 | no toss: format duel-wallclock: the runner plays both orders of the first server (match.first_server); format match-wallclock: you serve the first point |
